newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Products shipped from 1st Kyrgyzstan oil refinery.
newsitem.headline: Products shipped from 1st Kyrgyzstan oil refinery.

text.p: Kyrgyzstan's first oil refinery, financed by Canadian oil company Kyrgoil Corp, shipped its first oil products by truck on Monday, a spokesman for the venture said on Monday.
"The first cargoes went out by truck today," said Bill Arnold, special projects director for Texas-based Petrofac Corp which assembled the plant.

The refinery, constructed at a cost of $12 million with a 500,000-tonne annual capacity, is located in Jalalabad in the south of the mountainous and remote former Soviet republic. Kyrgoil and state oil company Kyrgyzneft are 50 percent partners in the refinery project.
Speaking by telephone from London, Arnold told Reuters that the refinery should produce 5,000 barrels per day (bpd) -- half capacity -- of oil products (mazut, diesel and gasoline) by next January.
"We're selling into the local (Kyrgyz) area," said Arnold, who added crude for the project would be sourced from existing but long neglected oil wells in the Fergana Valley.
He said Kyrgoil and Kyrgyzneft would increase current oil production from Fergana of 1,500 bpd to 25,000 bpd over four years.
